messages:
maria: FYI acme-x on Dedicated is requesting guidance for their token/queue limits. They see bursts up to ~5 requests/sec with occasional 512-token responses; p50 ~42ms p99 ~870ms on their pool. Can runtime suggest per-GPU token_budget + queue_depth and any kernel prefs?

samir: can you paste their current dedicated config and recent flamegraph?

maria: pasted below (from customer):

```
{
  "pool": "gpu-nv4-8",
  "kernel_policy": "auto",
  "token_budget_target": 2048,
  "max_queue_depth": 128,
  "kv_cache": { "per_session": true, "evict_policy": "lru" }
}
```

and the flame snippet (trimmed):

```
serving/runtime.cpp: kv_lookup 18%
attention_kernels: 44% (split: small-attn 28% / large-attn 16%)
io: 6%
batcher: 12% (queue wait ~60ms)
```

aj: k. couple quick thoughts: their token_budget_target is low for 512-token tails. With dedicated pools we tend to bias towards higher token budget to avoid forming lots of small dispatches. Also kernel_policy:auto is hitting small-attn kernel for seq>256 sometimes due to our selector bug — that raises latency.

aj: suggest initial tuning for acme-x: 
```
{
  "token_budget_target": "4096",       // target tokens per dispatch per-GPU
  "max_queue_depth": "64",            // limit concurrent queued requests per-worker
  "kernel_policy": "prefer_fp16_v2", // prefer newer kernel path for long seqs
  "kv_cache": "per_session:false"    // share cache across sessions to reduce misses
}
```

aj: rationale: bigger token budget reduces number of dispatches and amortizes kernel overhead; lower queue depth keeps queue wait bounded and backpressure to client; prefer_fp16_v2 avoids the slow codepath we saw.

olivia: noted the kernel selector regression — I have a patch that forces prefer_fp16_v2 for sequence_length >= 256 when model is llama2-like. It landed to staging earlier today. We should test on acme-x pool before rolling to prod.

infra-bot: Perf test run scheduled: test-id=acme-x-adjust-1760002345, workers=8, seeds=1000, variant=tokenflow-tune. ETA ~25m.

maria: can we run two variants for the customer: (A) token_budget=4096 / max_queue_depth=64 + kernel patch, (B) token_budget=8192 / max_queue_depth=32 (more aggressive). We can let them A/B for 2 hours and compare p99/token_cost.

samir: agree. Also watch KV cache hit rate; switching to shared cache can spike memory pressure — ensure evict_policy is sized: set kv_cache.max_entries=200k for their pool.

aj: add a small profiling harness snippet to collect per-dispatch metrics (tokens, wait_ms, exec_ms, kernel_tag):
```
# runtime profiling config
profiling: true
metrics: [tokens, queue_wait_ms, exec_ms, kernel_tag, kv_hit_rate]
report_interval_s: 60
```

jade-cs: acme-x expects minimal disruption. If perf regresses during the test we should be ready to rollback immediately and notify them. Also they asked for cost estimate delta — can infra approximate delta for token_budget increase?

aj: rough: token_budget doubling -> ~+10-18% tokenized compute cost but can reduce dispatch overhead -> could net out. We should compute per-hour with their workload after we collect test metrics.

olivia: I'll deploy the selector patch to the acme-x staging pool now and kick infra-bot run. maria, can you coordinate with jade to schedule the A/B window?

maria: will do. tagging @jade-cs : do you have a 2-hour window today at 16:00 UTC?

jade-cs: 16:00 UTC works for them. I'll confirm and add maintenance note.

infra-bot: test run started: test-id=acme-x-adjust-1760002345. Live metrics stream: https://perf.redwood/internal/tests/acme-x-adjust-1760002345

aj: one more note — if we see queue wait >120ms persistently, reduce token_budget_target stepwise by 25% until wait drops. If kernel_tag shows fallback-small-attn, force fallback disabled for the test to isolate effect.

samir: ack. I'll watch flamegraphs and memory.

maria: thanks team. I'll write up the recommended config and change request for acme-x once we have the first test run results. :thumbsup:
